campaign: safe-c33 shared-contract establishment (E2 follow-on: the X509_VERIFY_POLICY extension-method v2i config decoders)
subphase: B51 takes the 10 v2i config-decoder sites left BLOCKED by B50. Unlike the i2s/i2r print path, v2i is dispatched by do_ext_nconf (src/x509/v3_conf.rs:998-1107), not X509V3_EXT_print, and that dispatcher does NOT hold the registry read hold across the callback: X509V3_EXT_get_nid takes and releases the read hold before returning the borrowed row. B51 therefore adds fn-level # Safety contracts to the 10 callbacks and three end-to-end tests, and records the row-liveness obligation as the authority's borrowed-row ABI rather than adding a second lock or hold. No functional defect was found to be reachable through the dispatcher, so the source delta is contracts plus tests only (348 insertions, 0 deletions). The discharge is NOT applied: CAMPAIGN-STATUS.json is untouched and the closure was not run.

candidate.base_commit_subject: x509: hold the registry read lock across the v2i/i2d/d2i slots (B51 candidate)

authority.note: The authority builds STACK_OF(CONF_VALUE) from X509V3_parse_list(value) or NCONF_get_section(conf, value + 1), refuses NULL or empty, calls the first of v2i/s2i/r2i that is set, encodes the result through method->it or method->i2d, then frees it with method->ext_free or ASN1_item_free. The candidate's do_ext_nconf is the same shape; it adds no refusal the authority lacks except the guards recorded here. The brief's stated v2i signature (method, unsigned char **, long) and ext_free release belong to the d2i/print path, not to v2i; the actual slot is (method, X509V3_CTX *, STACK_OF(CONF_VALUE) *) and all ten rows release through `it` with ext_free NULL. That discrepancy is recorded in B51-R7 and is not silently repaired.

mechanism.discharge: SITE-SCOPED: the ten v2i boundaries below only. The mechanism state is unchanged and is not discharged mechanism-wide.

chosen_family.why: The closure has 11 BLOCKED obligations whose item is v2i-named: the ten below plus bitst_v2i. B50's not_touched taxonomy counts bitst_v2i under family bitst (2 = bitst_i2v + bitst_v2i), because bitst_v2i is a one-line forwarder to the same v2i_ASN1_BIT_STRING helper and usr_data table as its i2v sibling, so the campaign's v2i count is 10. B51 takes those ten. bitst_v2i stays BLOCKED in the bitst family and is NOT claimed here.

excluded.reason: Belongs to B50's bitst family (shared v2i_ASN1_BIT_STRING helper and usr_data table with bitst_i2v); outside the ten-site v2i scope. Remains BLOCKED, not claimed.

shared_contract: v2i slot contract stated on X509V3ExtMethod (src/x509/v3_lib.rs). do_ext_nconf resolves the row through X509V3_EXT_get_nid under a short registry read hold (src/x509/v3_conf.rs:1013) and uses the returned borrowed row after that hold is released; it refuses ext_nid == NID_undef (:1007), a NULL row (:1014), and a NULL or empty value stack (:1041); it builds STACK_OF(CONF_VALUE) from X509V3_parse_list (own, freed at :1060-1063) or NCONF_get_section (section-owned, not freed); it calls cb(method, ctx, nval) at :1059; on a non-NULL result it encodes through do_ext_i2d at :1098 and releases with ASN1_item_free(ext_struc, it()) at :1099-1101. The callback must consume `nval` read-only, must not free/retain it or its members, must not retain `method`/`ctx`, and must return a fresh object of exactly the row's `it` type, releasing any partial value itself on failure.

entry_points: X509V3_EXT_nconf_nid (src/x509/v3_conf.rs:1212) -> do_ext_nconf(:998); this is the entry the three tests drive.
X509V3_EXT_conf (src/x509/v3_conf.rs:1426) and X509V3_EXT_conf_nid (:1455) build a temporary NCONF and call the two above.
X509V3_EXT_add_nconf_sk (src/x509/v3_conf.rs:1245) walks a config section and calls X509V3_EXT_nconf_int(:1291).
dispatch_paths.lookup: X509V3_EXT_get_nid (src/x509/v3_lib.rs:748) takes a registry read hold for the lookup only and returns a BORROWED row; the hold is released at return (documented at :740-746). do_ext_nconf reads v2i/s2i/r2i/it/ext_free at :1020-1028.
dispatch_paths.values: at_section = (*value == '@') (:1031); X509V3_parse_list(value) (:1037) is an owning list the dispatcher frees after the call (:1060-1063); NCONF_get_section(conf, value + 1) (:1034) is a section-owned stack it must not free.
dispatch_paths.guard: nval.is_null() || OPENSSL_sk_num(nval) <= 0 is refused at :1041-1057 before any callback; this is the pre-slot guard the callback contracts rely on (B51-C1).
dispatch_paths.encode: do_ext_i2d(method, ext_nid, crit, ext_struc) at :1098; it uses method->it when set (:614-633) else method->i2d (:634-647).
dispatch_paths.free: ASN1_item_free(ext_struc, it()) at :1099-1101 when `it` is set; method->ext_free at :1102-1104 when it is not. All ten rows set `it` and ext_free is None.
dispatch_paths.lifetime: `method` is borrowed from X509V3_EXT_get_nid and is NOT protected by a read hold across the callback; `nval` is live across the call and is freed only after it when the dispatcher owns it; `ext_struc` is exclusively the dispatcher's from the callback return to :1098/:1101. The callback retains neither `method`, `nval`, nor its members.
dispatch_paths.allocator: ext_struc is a fresh value from the row's item allocator on the CRYPTO_* seam; the DER block is CRYPTO_malloc'd by ASN1_item_i2d and owned by do_ext_i2d's OwnedBuf (drop site :184). The dispatch itself allocates nothing beyond the parse list.
dispatch_paths.second_reader: The only production reads of a v2i slot are do_ext_nconf's :1020-1028. No test or other unit reads a v2i slot.
dispatch_paths.ctx: ctx is NULL or a live X509V3_CTX; do_ext_nconf does not check it. Only v2i_AUTHORITY_INFO_ACCESS forwards it (to v2i_GENERAL_NAME_ex, which documents NULL-or-live); the other nine ignore it.
dispatch_paths.retention: The callback may retain nothing. Its non-NULL result transfers to the dispatcher, which encodes it and releases it exactly once; a NULL result is reported as a failed extension build.

row_liveness.question: Does the registry read hold span the v2i dispatch, as it spans the i2s/i2r print path?
row_liveness.answer: YES, ENFORCED. B49/B50 relied on a hold in X509V3_EXT_print; the config-decode path had none, because X509V3_EXT_get_nid takes and releases the read lock at return. B51b adds RegistryReadGuard over the whole lookup-through-slot span in do_ext_nconf, X509V3_EXT_i2d and X509V3_EXT_d2i, so a concurrent X509V3_EXT_cleanup cannot release a DYNAMIC row under the callback. The duty is no longer documentary.
row_liveness.enforcement: src/x509/v3_conf.rs do_ext_nconf (~:1035), X509V3_EXT_i2d (~:742); src/x509/v3_lib.rs X509V3_EXT_d2i (~:892). RAII: RegistryReadGuard::Drop unlocks on every path, including early NULL returns.
row_liveness.observation: A #[cfg(test)] thread-local probe (v3_lib.rs read_hold_probe) is incremented by RegistryReadGuard::acquire and decremented by Drop; registry_read_held_on_this_thread() is absent from non-test builds and adds no exported item. A neutral control asserts the probe is false before dispatch, so true readings are not vacuous.
row_liveness.static_rows: The ten rows are process-lifetime pub static values reached through STANDARD_EXTS; X509V3_EXT_cleanup cannot release them.
row_liveness.dynamic_rows: X509V3_EXT_add_alias can copy a row containing a v2i slot into a DYNAMIC allocation released by ext_list_free; the added read hold now excludes that release for the whole dispatch.
row_liveness.caller_rows: X509V3_EXT_add still accepts a caller-owned row and the list borrows it (only DYNAMIC rows are freed). Caller storage lifetime stays a stated caller obligation (B51-R8); the registry lock does not and cannot protect the caller memory.

defect_class: uncontracted unsafe fn definitions at 10 X509_VERIFY_POLICY v2i sites. The blocks already carried per-line SAFETY comments but no fn-level # Safety. No functional defect was found reachable through do_ext_nconf: name is non-NULL from both producers (X509V3_parse_list checks `ntmp`; the config loader checks `(*v).name`), value is NULL-or-NUL-terminated, OPENSSL_sk_num/OPENSSL_sk_value are NULL-safe, OBJ_txt2obj/s2i_ASN1_INTEGER/X509V3_get_value_bool/int accept NULL, and the partial-value frees are correct. Two latent but unreachable hazards are recorded (B51-R3, B51-R4). The diff is therefore additive only.

boundaries.contract: v2i slot contract on X509V3ExtMethod. Caller do_ext_nconf's v2i arm (:1029-1066) establishes: method is a live borrowed row; nval is a live non-empty stack of live CONF_VALUE elements with non-NULL NUL-terminated name and NULL-or-NUL-terminated value; ctx is NULL or live. On success it returns a fresh ASIdentifiers owned by the dispatcher, encoded with ASIdentifiers_it and freed once with ASN1_item_free; on failure it frees the partial value. The returned type must match the row's `it` (registrar obligation). A concurrent X509V3_EXT_cleanup of a DYNAMIC row must not run during the call (B51-R1).

The `it` pairing is the registrar's obligation; a concurrent cleanup of a DYNAMIC row must not run during the call (B51-R1). Note: the closure still marks this operation's owning boundary ELIMINATED at a different coordinate (:146) while the source at :232 is still an uncontracted unsafe fn before this delta; B51 contracts it anyway and records the inconsistency in B51-R2.
established: do_ext_nconf refuses NID_undef/NULL row (:1007-1018).
do_ext_nconf refuses a NULL or empty values stack (:1041-1057).
Element name is non-NULL from both producers; value is NULL-or-NUL-terminated and the body falls back to name.
OPENSSL_strcasecmp/strtol are NULL-safe only after the fallback; name is non-NULL.
The result is encoded and released once with the row's own item (:1097-1105).
authority_derived: crypto/x509/v3_conf.c:96-112; crypto/x509/v3_tlsf.c:85-137.
The authority has no registry lock across the v2i call.

hidden_obligations_note: No obligation is hidden. The three obligations the callbacks do not enforce are stated in every contract above and enumerated as residuals: (1) a borrowed row must not be released concurrently (B51-R1); (2) the ASIdentifiers range parser assumes the config value fits in c_int (B51-R3); (3) the returned object's type must match the row's `it` (B51-R6). A hidden obligation is one that is neither enforced nor stated; none was found.
new_unsafe_assumptions_note: The delta adds documentation and tests only; no new unsafe operation or assumption was introduced. The tests call existing unsafe extern C APIs under per-call SAFETY comments and add no unsafe fn.
boundary_size: 10 callback bodies (unchanged), 10 fn-level # Safety contracts, one shared dispatcher arm (do_ext_nconf v2i branch, src/x509/v3_conf.rs:1029-1066), and 3 tests (two loops over all ten rows plus one pre-slot canary). No second lock or hold was added. B51b adds one structural hold mechanism (registry read guard on the config/i2d/d2i paths) shared by all ten sites, with three mutation-proven liveness canaries and one neutral control.
safe_callers_can_cause_ub_note: Every entry point that can reach a v2i callback is `unsafe extern "C"` (X509V3_EXT_nconf, X509V3_EXT_nconf_nid, X509V3_EXT_conf, X509V3_EXT_conf_nid, X509V3_EXT_add_nconf_sk). The callback type is Option<unsafe extern "C" fn>, and no safe Rust item accepts or returns X509V3ExtMethod. A safe Rust caller can therefore not reach these callbacks without an unsafe block; the C ABI obligations are stated in each contract.

negative_control.name: per-callback value-NULL guards are not independently mutation-canaried
negative_control.reason: These are authority-derived defensive checks, not the path that establishes the callbacks' preconditions. Removing the pmaps guard is behaviour-neutral (OBJ_txt2obj is NULL-safe and the next obj1/obj2 check still returns NULL), so a clean assertion cannot distinguish it; removing the asid guard would call strcmp on NULL and fault the harness rather than produce an assertion; the ist cnf.is_null() arm is unreachable because OPENSSL_sk_value answers NULL only out of range. They were therefore verified by contract review and exercised negatively by v2i_callbacks_reject_bad_values, not faked as mutation canaries. The producer-side non-NULL name checks (X509V3_parse_list checks ntmp; the config loader checks (*v).name) are shared by many units and are recorded as established facts by inspection.

residuals.description: Row liveness for DYNAMIC rows across the config-decode slot. Originally a documented caller duty (same class as the refused B46/B47 argument); now enforced by a read hold spanning the callback.
residuals.closed_by: B51b: RegistryReadGuard over do_ext_nconf, X509V3_EXT_i2d and X509V3_EXT_d2i, each with a mutation-proven liveness canary

residuals.description: The closure names 11 BLOCKED v2i-named obligations but B50's taxonomy counts v2i as 10 because bitst_v2i is grouped with bitst_i2v under family bitst. B51 follows the 10-site family and leaves bitst_v2i BLOCKED. Separately, v2i_TLS_FEATURE's owning boundary is recorded ELIMINATED at src/x509/v3_tlsf.rs:146 while the source at :232 was still an uncontracted unsafe fn before this delta; B51 contracts it and records the inconsistency rather than silently reclassifying it.

v2i_ASIdentifiers computes offset candidates with `strspn(...) as c_int` and then uses them as usize indices into the NUL-terminated value. A config value longer than INT_MAX would make the cast negative and the offset invalid. The authority has the same int cast. It is not reachable with any practical config value and cannot be given a failing test without a multi-gigabyte input, so it was not changed; the contract retains the input-length assumption.

X509v3_asid_add_id_or_range installs min/max into a fresh ASIdOrRange before OPENSSL_sk_push. If that push failed, the callee would free the range (and min/max), and v2i_ASIdentifiers's failure cleanup would free min/max again. The push cannot fail after OPENSSL_sk_reserve(list, 1) succeeds, so the branch is unreachable; no failing test can be written. Recorded, not changed.

Partial-decode ownership is exercised by v2i_callbacks_reject_bad_values but not proven leak-free: no allocator-hook or LeakSanitizer run was made, so a missing release in a failure path would not be detected.

The dispatcher encodes and frees the returned object with the row's `it` (ASN1_item_i2d / ASN1_item_free; all ten rows set `it` and ext_free is NULL). The callback must return exactly the item's type; a registrar that pairs a v2i callback with a mismatched `it` causes an invalid encode/free. That pairing is not checked by X509V3_EXT_add and is the registrar's obligation.

The subphase brief described v2i as `(X509V3_EXT_METHOD*, unsigned char**, long)` returning `*mut c_void` freed through `ext_free`, and pointed at X509V3_EXT_print. The actual v2i slot is `(const X509V3_EXT_METHOD*, X509V3_CTX*, STACK_OF(CONF_VALUE)*)`, dispatched by do_ext_nconf (v3_conf.c:79-135), and all ten rows are freed through `it` with ASN1_item_free, not ext_free. This receipt follows the code and the closure's v2i items; the brief's signature/release description is recorded here rather than silently adopted.

ctx may be NULL (do_ext_nconf's contract allows it and does not check it). Only v2i_AUTHORITY_INFO_ACCESS forwards ctx, to v2i_GENERAL_NAME_ex, which documents NULL-or-live; the other nine ignore it. A callback that begins reading ctx would inherit the caller's obligation to supply one.

test_harness_incident.what: The first liveness harness built an X509V3ExtMethod row as a helper local, passed &mut row to X509V3_EXT_add (which borrows the caller row by pointer), and returned the row by value. The registry kept a pointer into a dead frame.
test_harness_incident.observed: All three liveness tests failed at ext.is_null() (v3_conf.rs:1706/1734/1761) before reaching the probe; the gate reported FAILED 149 passed / 3 failed.
test_harness_incident.resolution: Box::leak in the #[cfg(test)] harness gives the row a static lifetime (dedicated test process; the registry borrows it; ext_flags stays non-DYNAMIC so X509V3_EXT_cleanup cannot free it). No assertion was weakened.
test_harness_incident.recorded_because: A vacuous or crashed liveness test cannot support a discharge; the failure and its fix are part of the evidence.
